figures.public_caption: Panel A illustrates the synthesis of Pdot−Qdot hybrid nanoparticles, where amine-functionalized PFBT is modified with thiols to bind to quantum dots, followed by nanoprecipitation with PS−PEG−COOH to form the final structure. Panel B shows TEM images of the resulting nanoparticles, with scale bars indicating size. Panel C presents a histogram of their hydrodynamic diameters measured by DLS.

figures.public_caption: Panel A shows the UV−vis spectrum of Pdot−Qdot nanoparticles in water. Panel B compares emission spectra of QD655, QD705, and QD800 in decane and their corresponding Pdot−Qdot forms. Panels C and D display single-particle fluorescence images and intensity distributions for PFBT−DBT Pdots and PFBT−QD655 Pdot−Qdot NPs, with scale bars and histogram data from over 700 particles.

general_background.title: Ligands in solution and at surfaces
general_background.summary: Ligands can associate with dissolved species and particle surfaces, affecting their interactions with the surrounding liquid. A ligand shell compatible with the solvent can provide a barrier to close particle approach, helping a dispersion resist aggregation.
